data.gender_notes: Ayanin is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ayanin is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Ayana', which means 'direction' or 'goal'. The suffix '-in' denotes 'Lord of'. Thus, Ayanin can be translated as 'Lord of the Vedas'. The Vedas are the oldest and most sacred texts of Hinduism, and are considered the foundation of Hindu philosophy. The name Ayanin carries the meaning “Lord of the Vedas” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ayanin usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the vedas and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes wisdom, knowledge, and spiritual guidance.
data.etymology: Ayanin belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Vedas.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ayanin total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.
